THIS CRIMINAL APPEAL COMING ON FOR HEARING THIS DAY, B.VEERAPPA J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The appellant/accused has filed the present criminal appeal against the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 5/6-09.2017 made in S.C. No.5007/2015 on the file of the III Addl. District & Sessions Judge, Mandya (sitting at Srirangapattana) convicting and sentencing him for the offences punishable under the provisions of Sections 498A and 302 of IPC.
2.

sentences.text: By the impugned judgment, the trial Court sentenced the appellant/accused to undergo imprisonment for life for the offence punishable under Section 302 of IPC and sentenced him to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for two years for the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC with fine and default clauses.
3. It is the case of the prosecution that the marriage of the deceased and the accused was solemnized about 20 years prior to the incident.
Out of the wedlock, PW.1/Madhu and PW.11/Meghana were born and they are aged about 19 years and 17 years as on the date of the incident.

On 21.5.2014 at 11 p.m., the accused, in his house at Haralahally village assaulted his wife Renuka, who was sleeping on the cot, by suspecting her fidelity and further abusing her that, she has lost character and she shall not be allowed to survive and with an intention to commit her murder, assaulted her by Axe, above the right ear, caused fatal injuries and she succumbed to the injuries on 8.9.2014 at K.R. Hospital,
Mysuru.
Accordingly, PW.1/H.M. Madhu, who is the son of the accused and the deceased lodged complaint before the SHO, Pandavapura.
PW.12/Head Constable - H.K. Raghu registered the case in Crime No.211/201 against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 and 307 of IPC and filed FIR as per Ex.P10.
Thereafter, investigation was handed over to PW.16, the then PSI, Pandavapura.
After investigation, the Investigating Authority initially filed the charge sheet against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 and 307 of IPC.
In view of death of the deceased, Section 307 was converted into Section 302 of IPC.

The learned Magistrate took the congisance and referred the matter to the learned Sessions Judge, who secured the presence of the accused and framed the charge under Sections 498A, 504 and 302 of IPC.
The charge was read over and explained to the accused in the language known to him, who denied the allegations made and claimed to be tried.

4. In order to prove the guilt of the accused, the prosecution examined in all, 18 witnesses as PWs.1 to 18 and got marked the material documents - Ex.P1 to Ex.P22 and the material objects - MOs.1 to Mahesha vs State Of Karnataka on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104258093/
2 5.
5.
After completion of evidence of the prosecution witnesses, the statement of the accused was recorded as contemplated under the provisions of Section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
The accused denied all the incriminating circumstances that were found against him in the evidence of the prosecution witnesses.

The accused has not chosen to lead any defence evidence, but got marked the documents as per Ex.D1/portion of the complaint - Ex.P1; Ex.D2/portion of the complainant statement; Ex.D3/portion of Ex.P6; and Ex.D4/portion of Ex.P1.
6.

Based on the pleadings, the learned Sessions Judge has formulated following points for consideration:
1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that, on 21.5.2014 at 11 p.m., at Haralahally Village, in the residential house of accused, by suspecting his wife Renuka's fidelity, accused abused her in a filthy language thereby gave provocation to her intending or knowing it to be likely that such provocation will cause Renuka to break public peace and thereby, committed offence punishable U/S.504 of the IPC?

2. Whether prosecution further proves beyond reasonable doubt that on the above said date, time and place, accused subjected Renuka to mental and physical cruelty being her husband and assaulted her with Axe on her ear and thereby, committed offence punishable Under section 498A of the IPC?

3. Whether prosecution further proves beyond reasonable doubt that on the above said date, time and place, accused committed murder intentionally causing death of Renuka by assaulting her with an Axe on her ear when she was asleep on a Cot and she succumbed to the injuries on 08.09.2014 at 6-20 p.m., in K.R.Hospital, Mysuru and thereby, committed offence punishable under section 302 of the IPC?
7.

Considering both the oral and documentary evidence on record, the learned Sessions Judge answered point No.1 in the negative holding that the prosecution failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that on 21.5.2014 at 11 p.m., at Haralahally village, in the residential house of accused, by suspecting his wife Renuka's fidelity, accused abused her in a filthy language, thereby gave provocation to her intending or knowing it to be likely that such provocation will cause Renuka to break public peace and thereby failed to prove that the accused committed an offence punishable under Section 504 of IPC.

The learned Sessions Judge answered point No.2 in the affirmative holding that the prosecution proved beyond reasonable doubt that on the above said date, time and place, accused subjected Renuka to mental and physical cruelty being her husband and assaulted her with Axe on her ear and thereby, committed an offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC.

The learned Sessions Judge answered point No.3 in the affirmative holding that the prosecution proved beyond reasonable doubt that on the above said date, time and place, accused committed murder intentionally causing death of Renuka by assaulting her with an Axe on her ear when she was asleep on a cot and she succumbed to the injuries on 8.9.2014 at 6.20 p.m., in K.R. Hopsital,

sentences.text: Hence, the present criminal appeal is filed by the appellant/accused.
8. The State has not filed any appeal against the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence insofar as acquitting the accused for the offence punishable under Section 504 of IPC.
9. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties.

10. Sri C. Parameshwarappa, learned counsel for the appellant/accused contended with vehemence that the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the learned Sessions Judge, convicting and sentencing the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 302 and 498A of IPC, is erroneous, contrary to the material on record, cannot be sustained and liable to be set aside.
The learned Sessions Judge proceeded to convict the accused mainly relying upon the evidence of the prosecution witnesses, which is highly interested, contradictory, unreliable and artificial.
He further contended that there are no eye witnesses and direct evidence against the appellant.
In the circumstances, the impugned judgment cannot be sustained and liable to be set aside.

Alternatively, learned counsel would contend that as per Ex.P1/complaint, there was altercation between the accused and the deceased with regard to selling of cattle, thereby the accused lost self control and the unfortunate incident occurred.
Though the incident occurred on 21.5.2014, the deceased died on 8.9.2014 after a lapse of nearly three months.
The unfortunate incident occurred without premeditation and therefore, at the most the case would fall under Section 304 Part I of IPC and not under Section 302 of IPC.

Therefore, learned counsel sought for modification of the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence and to reduce the sentence taking into consideration that the accused has a responsibility to look after his children and other mitigating circumstances.
11.

Per contra, Sri Vijaykumar Majage, learned Addl. SPP while justifying the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence would contend that the motive for the murder of the deceased, who is none other than wife of the accused is that he was suspecting her fidelity, thereby he murdered the deceased.
The same was specifically stated by the eye witnesses viz., PW.1 (son of the accused and the deceased) and PW.11 (daughter of the deceased).
Based on the oral and documentary evidence on record, the learned Sessions Judge rightly proceeded to convict the accused.
Therefore, he sought to dismiss the appeal.

12. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for the parties, the only point that would arise for our consideration in the present appeal is:
"Whether the appellant/accused has made out a case to interfere with the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence insofar as convicting and sentencing him for the offences punishable under Sections 302 and 498A of IPC in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case ?"

14. The material on record clearly depicts that the marriage between the accused and deceased was performed - 20 - about 20 years prior to the incident.
It is also not in dispute that out of the wedlock PW.1-son and PW.11-daughter were born.
PW.1, son of the deceased and accused is the eye- witness to the incident who admitted his deceased mother to the hospital.
Nothing has been elicited in his examination or cross-examination to disbelieve the version of PW.1 that his father/accused is involved in the homicidal death of deceased Renuka.
PW.11-daughter of deceased has specifically stated that her father used to suspect the fidelity of her mother and used to quarrel with her for money.
She has further stated that on the date of the unfortunate incident, i.e, on 21.05.2014, he was drunk and assaulted her mother with an axe.
Later, she was taken to Pandavapura Government Hospital.

From there, she was shifted to St. Joseph Hospital, Mysore and later, she was shifted to K.R.Hospital,
Mysore and died in K.R.Hospital due to severe head injuries.
15. PWs.2 to 4-independent witnesses have initially supported the case of the prosecution, but in the cross- examination, they have not supported the case of the prosecution.

PW.5-Dr.Parashivamurthy,
who was working as Medical Officer in St.Joseph Hospital, Mysore on the date of the Mahesha vs State Of Karnataka on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104258093/

She was further treated by Dr.Goutham, Neurologist and operated for head injuries.
However, relatives of the deceased got her discharged from the hospital against medical advice, stating that they are unable to bear the expenses for treatment.
He has issued wound certificate at Ex.P5.
He has specifically stated that surgery was conducted for elevation of depressed fraction and wound debridement was done on 22.05.2014.

P.W.7-Dr.Chandrashekar has deposed that on 30.06.2014, injured Renuka was brought to K.R.Hospital for follow up treatment and she was in unconscious state.

she would have survived.

PW.1 and PW11, children of deceased Renuka have deposed that their father used to assault their mother for money and on the date of incident, he assaulted their mother with axe with an intention to kill her,
by suspecting her fidelity after leading 20 years of married life with her.
There was an - 23 - altercation between Renuka and accused in the matter of sale proceeds of cattle.

Therefore, this is not a case to impose punishment of imprisonment for life and the case falls under Exception 1 of Section 300 of IPC, which reads as under:
Section 300: Murder:
xxx xxx xxx xxx Exception I - When culpable homicide is not murder.--Culpable homicide is not murder if the offender whilst deprived of self-control by grave and Mahesha vs State Of Karnataka on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104258093/
9 sudden provocation, causes the death of the person who gave the provocation or causes the death of any other person by mistake or accident.

18. A careful perusal of the said provision makes it clear that culpable homicide does not amount to murder if the offender whilst deprived of self-control by grave and sudden provocation, causes the death of the person who gave the provocation or causes the death of any other person by mistake or accident.

In the present case, as stated supra, on 21.05.2014, there was an altercation between the accused and deceased in the matter of sale proceeds of cattle and the accused assaulted the deceased with an axe.
Later, she was - 24 - shifted to hospital and she died about 3 months after the incident.

P.W.1 and P.W.11, children of deceased have categorically deposed that the accused was under the influence of alcohol and an altercation took place between them in the matter of sale proceeds of a cattle.
The accused lost self-control and assaulted the deceased Renuka with axe.
The said aspect has not been considered by the learned Sessions Judge.
Therefore, it amounts to culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
19. The material on record clearly depicts that the accused used to assault the deceased even prior to the incident demanding money.
He was in a drunken state on the date of the incident.
There was an altercation between accused and deceased and he assaulted the deceased with an axe.
Even in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C., he has not explained the cause for the death of his wife deceased Renuka.

In the light of the provisions of Section 106 of the Evidence Act and since the accused has not taken any defence in respect of the voluntary statement made by him, adverse inference has to be taken against the accused that the death of the deceased was at the instance of the accused.

- 25 - 20.Our view is fortified by the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Prahlad -vs- State of Rajasthan reported in (2020)1 SCC (Crl.) 381, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court held at paragraph-11 as under:

sentences.text: No explanation is forthcoming from the statement of the accused under Section 313 CrPC as to when he parted the company of the victim.
Also, no explanation is there as to what happened after getting the chocolates for the victim.
The silence on the part of the accused, in such a matter wherein he is expected to come out with an explanation, leads to an adverse inference against the accused.
21. The material on record clearly depicts that from the evidence of PW.1-son, it is evident that there was an altercation between accused and deceased and accused was under the influence of alcohol.
The accused lost control and assaulted the deceased with an axe.
The accused had led marital life for 20 years with the deceased and they were living with two children.

Therefore, it is a fit case where Mahesha vs State Of Karnataka on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104258093/
10 the conviction of the accused for the offence under Section 302 of IPC has to be modified and altered into one under Section 304 Part I of IPC with fine.
- 26 - 22.

For the reasons stated supra, the point raised in the present appeal has to be answered partly in the affirmative holding that the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the trial Court calls for modification and the impugned judgment convicting the appellant/accused for the offence punishable under Section 302 of IPC has to be modified and altered into one under Section 304 Part I of IPC and the appellant/accused shall be sentenced to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for a period of TEN YEARS and to pay a fine of Rs.1,00,000/- and in default of payment of fine to undergo Simple Imprisonment for a period of two years, in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case.
23.

In view of the above, we pass the following order:
ORDER i) The Criminal Appeal filed by the appellant/accused is allowed in part.
ii) The impugned Judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 05.09.2017 made in S.C. No.5007/2015 on the file of the III Addl. District &
- 27 -  Sessions Judge, Mandya (sitting at  Srirangapattana) convicting the  appellant - accused for the offence  punishable under Section 302 of IPC  and sentencing him to undergo imprisonment for life and to pay fine of Rs.10,000/- is hereby modified.

iii) The appellant/accused is hereby convicted for the offence punishable under Section 304 Part I of IPC and sentenced to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for a period of TEN YEARS and to pay a fine of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh only only) and in default of payment of fine, he shall undergo Simple Imprisonment for a period of two years.
iv) The appellant - accused is entitled to the benefit of set off as contemplated under the provisions of Section 428 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

vi)

opennyai_summary.facts:
By the impugned judgment, the trial Court sentenced the appellant/accused to undergo imprisonment for life for the offence punishable under Section 302 of IPC and sentenced him to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for two years for the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC with fine and default clauses.
After investigation, the Investigating Authority initially filed the charge sheet against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 and 307 of IPC.
In view of death of the deceased, Section 307 was converted into Section 302 of IPC.
The learned Magistrate took the congisance and referred the matter to the learned Sessions Judge, who secured the presence of the accused and framed the charge under Sections 498A, 504 and 302 of IPC.
The charge was read over and explained to the accused in the language known to him, who denied the allegations made and claimed to be tried.
After completion of evidence of the prosecution witnesses, the statement of the accused was recorded as contemplated under the provisions of Section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
The learned Sessions Judge answered point No.2 in the affirmative holding that the prosecution proved beyond reasonable doubt that on the above said date, time and place, accused subjected Renuka to mental and physical cruelty being her husband and assaulted her with Axe on her ear and thereby, committed an offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC.
The learned Sessions Judge answered point No.3 in the affirmative holding that the prosecution proved beyond reasonable doubt that on the above said date, time and place, accused committed murder intentionally causing death of Renuka by assaulting her with an Axe on her ear when she was asleep on a cot and she succumbed to the injuries on 8.9.2014 at 6.20 p.m., in K.R. 8. The State has not filed any appeal against the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence insofar as acquitting the accused for the offence punishable under Section 504 of IPC.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Based on the pleadings, the learned Sessions Judge has formulated following points for consideration:
1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that, on 21.5.2014 at 11 p.m., at Haralahally Village, in the residential house of accused, by suspecting his wife Renuka's fidelity, accused abused her in a filthy language thereby gave provocation to her intending or knowing it to be likely that such provocation will cause Renuka to break public peace and thereby, committed offence punishable U/S.504 of the IPC?
2. Whether prosecution further proves beyond reasonable doubt that on the above said date, time and place, accused subjected Renuka to mental and physical cruelty being her husband and assaulted her with Axe on her ear and thereby, committed offence punishable Under section 498A of the IPC?
3. Whether prosecution further proves beyond reasonable doubt that on the above said date, time and place, accused committed murder intentionally causing death of Renuka by assaulting her with an Axe on her ear when she was asleep on a Cot and she succumbed to the injuries on 08.09.2014 at 6-20 p.m., in K.R.Hospital, Mysuru and thereby, committed offence punishable under section 302 of the IPC?
7.
Considering both the oral and documentary evidence on record, the learned Sessions Judge answered point No.1 in the negative holding that the prosecution failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that on 21.5.2014 at 11 p.m., at Haralahally village, in the residential house of accused, by suspecting his wife Renuka's fidelity, accused abused her in a filthy language, thereby gave provocation to her intending or knowing it to be likely that such provocation will cause Renuka to break public peace and thereby failed to prove that the accused committed an offence punishable under Section 504 of IPC.
12. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for the parties, the only point that would arise for our consideration in the present appeal is:
"Whether the appellant/accused has made out a case to interfere with the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence insofar as convicting and sentencing him for the offences punishable under Sections 302 and 498A of IPC in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case ?"
opennyai_summary.arguments:
10. Sri C. Parameshwarappa, learned counsel for the appellant/accused contended with vehemence that the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the learned Sessions Judge, convicting and sentencing the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 302 and 498A of IPC, is erroneous, contrary to the material on record, cannot be sustained and liable to be set aside.
The learned Sessions Judge proceeded to convict the accused mainly relying upon the evidence of the prosecution witnesses, which is highly interested, contradictory, unreliable and artificial.
Though the incident occurred on 21.5.2014, the deceased died on 8.9.2014 after a lapse of nearly three months.
The unfortunate incident occurred without premeditation and therefore, at the most the case would fall under Section 304 Part I of IPC and not under Section 302 of IPC.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
There was an - 23 - altercation between Renuka and accused in the matter of sale proceeds of cattle.
Therefore, this is not a case to impose punishment of imprisonment for life and the case falls under Exception 1 of Section 300 of IPC, which reads as under:
Section 300: Murder:
xxx xxx xxx xxx Exception I - When culpable homicide is not murder.--Culpable homicide is not murder if the offender whilst deprived of self-control by grave and Mahesha vs State Of Karnataka on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104258093/
9 sudden provocation, causes the death of the person who gave the provocation or causes the death of any other person by mistake or accident.
18. A careful perusal of the said provision makes it clear that culpable homicide does not amount to murder if the offender whilst deprived of self-control by grave and sudden provocation, causes the death of the person who gave the provocation or causes the death of any other person by mistake or accident.
In the present case, as stated supra, on 21.05.2014, there was an altercation between the accused and deceased in the matter of sale proceeds of cattle and the accused assaulted the deceased with an axe.
Later, she was - 24 - shifted to hospital and she died about 3 months after the incident.
P.W.1 and P.W.11, children of deceased have categorically deposed that the accused was under the influence of alcohol and an altercation took place between them in the matter of sale proceeds of a cattle.
The accused lost self-control and assaulted the deceased Renuka with axe.
Therefore, it amounts to culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
19. The material on record clearly depicts that the accused used to assault the deceased even prior to the incident demanding money.
He was in a drunken state on the date of the incident.
There was an altercation between accused and deceased and he assaulted the deceased with an axe.
Even in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C., he has not explained the cause for the death of his wife deceased Renuka.
In the light of the provisions of Section 106 of the Evidence Act and since the accused has not taken any defence in respect of the voluntary statement made by him, adverse inference has to be taken against the accused that the death of the deceased was at the instance of the accused.
For the reasons stated supra, the point raised in the present appeal has to be answered partly in the affirmative holding that the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the trial Court calls for modification and the impugned judgment convicting the appellant/accused for the offence punishable under Section 302 of IPC has to be modified and altered into one under Section 304 Part I of IPC and the appellant/accused shall be sentenced to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for a period of TEN YEARS and to pay a fine of Rs.1,00,000/- and in default of payment of fine to undergo Simple Imprisonment for a period of two years, in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case.
